meta.title: 12-Week Plan
meta.priority: Run 5 km. The gym work supports the running and rebuilds the quad.
meta.disclaimer: This is a training plan, not medical advice. It does not diagnose or treat the quad problem. If symptoms worsen or match a 'stop and get it checked' sign, see a GP or physiotherapist.

notes: Ask gym staff for a machine induction - they will set the machines up for your height.
Weeks 1-2: do 2 sets of every exercise, not 3. Start light and find your weights.
Record your starting bodyweight, waist, plank hold and quad stretch test.
Still 2 sets of everything.
Record this week's working weights for Leg Press, Chest Press and Seated Row - this is your strength baseline.
Move up to the full sets listed.
Lighter week: one set fewer on everything; keep weights the same. Let your body catch up.
Measure your waist.
Phase 2 starts: new exercises - ask staff to check your goblet squat and Romanian deadlift.
Friday's cardio becomes a short run.
Kicking Stage 1 starts. Record your first kick pain score.

Fri 1 Jan: check your gym's holiday hours. If closed, do Friday's session on Thu 31 Dec.

Wednesday: one set fewer on everything.
Friday: upper body only and 10 min easy cross trainer - no leg work.

running.pace: Easy: you can talk in sentences. Around 6:00-7:30 per km is fine - slower is better than faster.
running.rule: Follow the time, not the distance. If a week went badly (amber or red), repeat it before moving on.
running.strides: Strides = 15-20 seconds of relaxed, faster running (not a sprint), with a full walk back. Only on green weeks. They are the first step back towards sprinting.
saturday_warmup: Leg swings forwards and back - 10 each leg
Leg swings side to side - 10 each leg
Walking lunges - 10 steps (small steps at first)

kicking.rule: Kick after the Saturday warm-up and BEFORE the run - a tired quad is more easily strained. Move up a stage only after two green sessions in a row. If amber, repeat the stage. If red, drop back a stage. Stages can take longer than the weeks shown - that is fine.

stages.name: No ball yet
stages.what: Build quad strength in the gym. Do the Saturday warm-up and the quad stretch test only.

stages.name: Short side-foot passes
stages.what: Side-foot passes over 10-15 m against a wall or with a friend. 2 x 15 passes with each foot.

stages.name: Longer passes
stages.what: Side-foot and laces passes over 20-30 m at about half power. 2 x 15 with each foot.

stages.name: Driven passes
stages.what: Driven passes and shots at about 70% power. 2 x 10 with the kicking leg, plus easy passes with the other.

stages.name: Full strikes
stages.what: Build to full-power strikes: 5 at 80%, then 5 at 90-100%. Only if Stage 3 was green twice in a row.

traffic_light.how: Rate quad pain 0-10 during each run, kick session and leg exercise, and again the next morning. 0 = nothing, 10 = worst imaginable.

green.meaning: Fine. Carry on. Progress if the last two sessions were green.

amber.meaning: Finish at an easier level. Do not progress next time - repeat the step.

red.range: 5+, or sharp pain, or worse the next morning
red.meaning: Stop that activity today. Next time, drop back one step.

traffic_light.next_morning: If the quad is clearly stiffer or sorer than usual the next morning, treat the session as amber.
traffic_light.stretch_test: Quad stretch test - every Sunday, and before any reverse Nordic: standing quad stretch on the affected leg, gentle, 20 seconds. Rate the pain 0-10.

stop_and_seek_advice: A sudden sharp pain, a 'pop' or a 'pull' while kicking, sprinting or lifting.
Swelling or bruising on the thigh.
Limping, or pain walking or on the stairs.
Pain at rest or at night.
Two red days in any two-week period, or symptoms getting worse over two weeks.
Chest pain, feeling faint or dizzy, or unusual breathlessness during exercise - stop and speak to a GP.

lifting.starting_weights: Week 1: start with a weight you could lift 15+ times. Over the first two weeks, nudge it up until the listed reps feel moderately hard with 2-3 reps left in the tank.
lifting.progression: Double progression: when you complete every set at the TOP of the rep range with 2-3 reps left in the tank, add the smallest weight step next time. If you can't reach the bottom of the range, go back down a step.
lifting.reps_in_reserve: 'Reps left in the tank' = how many more good reps you could have done. Aim for 2-3. Never grind to failure.
lifting.machines: Write down seat and pad settings. Machine weights are not comparable between different machines or gyms, so compare like with like.
lifting.technique: Controlled technique matters more than lifting heavier.

effort_scale.label: Moderate
effort_scale.feel: Working, but could still talk in sentences

effort_scale.label: Maximum
effort_scale.feel: Couldn't do any more - avoid in this plan

body.weigh_in: Once a week, same morning, after the toilet, before eating. Sunday works well.
body.waist: Weeks 1, 4, 8 and 12. Tape measure around your belly button, relaxed, after breathing out.
protein: Have a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal (3 meals, plus a snack on gym days).
Good sources: eggs, Greek yoghurt, milk, chicken, fish, lean meat, beans, lentils, tofu, cottage cheese.
Rough daily guide for adults strength training: 1.2-1.6 g of protein per kg of bodyweight (for example, at 80 kg that's about 95-130 g a day). No need to count exactly.
other: Eat something with carbohydrate 1-3 hours before a run (toast, banana, porridge).
Drink water through the day - more on sauna days.
Aim for 7+ hours of sleep. It is when you get stronger.

bike.name: Exercise Bike
bike.what: Warms up your legs and gently raises your heart rate before training.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent when the pedal is at the bottom.
Pedal at an easy pace - you should be able to chat.
For the last 2 minutes, pedal a little faster.
tips: You should finish warmer, not tired.

treadmill_run.name: Treadmill Run
treadmill_run.what: Your Monday (and from Week 5, Friday) run. A treadmill gives an even surface and makes it easy to control speed.
steps: Clip the safety key to your clothing.
Walk briskly for 2 minutes to warm up.
Raise the speed to an easy jog. Start around 8-10 km/h (6:00-7:30 per km) - slower is fine.
Follow this week's run/walk pattern. For walk breaks, drop to a brisk walk.
Set the incline to 1% - it feels closer to running outdoors.
tips: Easy means you could still talk in sentences.
Short, light steps. Hold the rails only to get on and off.
treadmill_run.cue: Easy, chatty pace. Short light steps

outdoor_run.name: Saturday Run (outdoors)
outdoor_run.equipment: Trainers, a flat route, a phone or watch for timing
outdoor_run.what: Your key run of the week. This is the one that builds towards 5 km.
steps: Walk briskly for 5 minutes.
Do the Saturday warm-up (see below) - and kicking practice if it is on this week.
Run this week's pattern at an easy, chatty pace.
Walk for 5 minutes to cool down.
tips: Choose a flat loop in the park so you can stop at any point.
If your phone or watch records distance, log it - but time is what the plan follows.
outdoor_run.cue: Flat loop, easy pace, walk 5 min after

cross_trainer.name: Cross Trainer
cross_trainer.what: Running-like movement with no impact - kind to the quad.
steps: Step on, hold the moving handles and start pedalling slowly.
Settle into an easy-to-moderate pace for the set time.
Push and pull the handles to use your arms too.
tips: Stand tall - avoid leaning on the handles.

swim.name: Swim
swim.what: Whole-body fitness with zero impact. Wednesday's structured set, mostly front crawl.
steps: Warm up: 2 easy lengths of backstroke.
Main set: this week's front crawl lengths (see the session), resting at the wall between them.
Swim the main set 'comfortably hard': about 6 out of 10, breathing hard but in control.
Cool down: 2 easy lengths of backstroke.
tips: Breaststroke only as an easy recovery length, and only if your knee is happy: its kick strains the inside of the knee.
If front crawl breathing is hard, swap a length for backstroke. Rest longer rather than stopping.
swim.cue: Front crawl lengths, rest at the wall

leg_press.name: Leg Press
leg_press.what: Strengthens the front and back of your thighs and your bottom. Your main leg exercise.
steps: Sit with your back flat against the pad.
Place your feet hip-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Push the platform up slightly and release the safety handles.
Bend your knees slowly until they are at about a right angle (or as far as is comfortable).
Push through your whole foot to straighten - stop just before your knees lock.
Put the safety handles back on when you finish.
tips: Keep your lower back on the pad throughout.
Knees stay in line with your toes - don't let them cave in.
leg_press.cue: Push the platform away. Don't lock knees

leg_extension.name: Leg Extension
leg_extension.what: Works the front-thigh (quad) muscles directly - the area you are rebuilding.
steps: Sit with your back against the pad. Line your knee up with the machine's pivot (often marked with a dot).
Set the roller on the front of your lower shins, just above the ankles.
Straighten your legs over about 2 seconds and pause briefly.
Lower slowly over 3 seconds.
tips: Start very light. This loads the quad directly, so use the traffic-light rules.
Hold the side handles and keep your hips down on the seat.

chest_press.name: Chest Press
chest_press.what: Strengthens chest, shoulders and the back of the arms.
steps: Set the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest.
Sit back against the pad and grip the handles.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until your hands are near your chest.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and down - don't shrug.
chest_press.cue: Push forward, return slowly. Shoulders down

seated_row.name: Seated Row
seated_row.equipment: Seated row machine or low cable with a handle
seated_row.what: Strengthens your upper back - balances the chest press and helps posture.
steps: Sit tall with your chest against the pad (machine) or knees soft (cable).
Pull the handles towards your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together gently.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Don't round your back or lean back to pull.
seated_row.cue: Pull to lower ribs. Sit tall

leg_curl.name: Leg Curl
leg_curl.equipment: Seated or lying leg curl machine
leg_curl.what: Strengthens the back of your thighs (hamstrings) - important for running and kicking.
steps: Line your knee up with the machine's pivot.
Set the padded roller just above your heels.
Bend your knees to move the roller towards the back of your thighs.
Straighten slowly.
tips: Smooth and controlled - don't swing the weight.
leg_curl.cue: Bend knees to pull the pad under. Return slowly

lat_pulldown.name: Lat Pulldown
lat_pulldown.what: Strengthens your upper back and the sides of your back.
steps: Adjust the thigh pad so your legs are held firmly.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder-width.
Lean back very slightly and pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Never pull the bar behind your neck.
Don't swing your body to move the weight.
lat_pulldown.cue: Pull bar to upper chest. Never behind neck

shoulder_press.name: Shoulder Press
shoulder_press.what: Strengthens your shoulders and the back of your arms.
steps: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Press the handles upwards through a comfortable range.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
tips: Don't lock your elbows hard at the top.
Keep your back against the pad.
shoulder_press.cue: Press up, lower slowly to shoulders

cable_knee_drive.name: Cable Knee Drive
cable_knee_drive.equipment: Low cable pulley with an ankle strap
cable_knee_drive.what: Strengthens the hip flexor and upper front thigh - the muscles that swing your leg into a kick.
steps: Attach the ankle strap to the low pulley and to one ankle.
Stand facing away from the machine, holding something steady.
Drive your knee forwards and up to hip height.
Lower slowly. Do all reps, then switch legs.
tips: Start very light - this is a kicking-specific muscle.
No ankle strap? Do slow standing knee raises with no weight.
cable_knee_drive.cue: Drive knee to hip height, lower slowly

plank.name: Plank
plank.what: Strengthens your core (stomach and lower back muscles) to keep your body steady when running.
steps: Lie face down. Place your elbows under your shoulders.
Lift your body onto your forearms and toes (or knees for an easier version).
Hold a straight line from shoulders to heels (or knees).
Breathe normally. Stop when your hips start to sag.
tips: Quality over time - stop before your lower back sags.
plank.cue: Straight line. Stop before hips sag

side_plank.name: Side Plank
side_plank.what: Strengthens the sides of your core and hips - helps you run without wobbling.
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder.
Bend your knees (easier) or keep your legs straight.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line. Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips pushed forward, not sticking out behind.
side_plank.cue: Lift hips into a straight line

dead_bug.name: Dead Bug
dead_bug.what: A gentle core exercise that teaches you to keep your lower back steady.
steps: Lie on your back. Arms straight up, knees bent at a right angle above your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor.
Slowly lower one arm behind you and the opposite leg towards the floor.
Return and switch sides. That is one rep each side.
tips: Move slowly. Breathe out as you lower.
dead_bug.cue: Back pressed down. Lower opposite arm + leg

glute_bridge.name: Glute Bridge
glute_bridge.what: Strengthens your bottom (glutes) and hamstrings - key running muscles.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Squeeze your bottom and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a line.
Pause for 1 second, then lower slowly.
tips: Push through your heels. Don't arch your lower back at the top.

calf_raise.name: Calf Raise
calf_raise.equipment: A step or the floor, a rail to hold
calf_raise.what: Strengthens your calves and ankles. Runners need strong calves.
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step, holding a rail.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can. Pause.
Lower your heels slowly below the step.
Weeks 9-12: do it on one leg at a time.
tips: Slow on the way down - count 3 seconds.
calf_raise.cue: Up on toes, lower heels slowly

farmer_carry.name: Farmer Carry
farmer_carry.equipment: Two dumbbells or kettlebells, clear floor space
farmer_carry.what: Builds grip, core and whole-body strength. Teaches you to stay tall under load.
steps: Bend your knees and pick up a weight in each hand with a flat back.
Stand tall with your shoulders level.
Walk steadily for the set time.
Bend your knees to put the weights down.
tips: Choose a weight that is heavy but lets you walk without leaning.
farmer_carry.cue: Weight in each hand. Walk tall

goblet_squat.name: Goblet Squat
goblet_squat.what: A squat holding a weight at your chest. Builds leg strength and mobility.
steps: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest, gripping the top end.
Stand with feet slightly wider than your hips, toes turned out a little.
Sit down between your heels as low as is comfortable.
Push through your feet to stand up.
tips: Keep your chest up.
Squatting down to a bench is a good way to learn the depth. No weight is fine at first.
goblet_squat.cue: Weight at chest. Sit down between heels

split_squat.name: Split Squat
split_squat.equipment: Floor space (later two dumbbells), a rail for balance
split_squat.what: Single-leg strength. Running is a single-leg sport - this is great preparation.
steps: Stand with one foot forward and one back, about a stride apart. Back heel lifted.
Lower your back knee straight down towards the floor - stop just above it.
Push through your front foot to rise.
Do all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Hold a rail at first. Weeks 9-12: hold dumbbells.
Keep your body upright. Shorten the range if the front thigh complains.
split_squat.cue: Back knee down, push through front foot

db_rdl.name: Romanian Deadlift (dumbbells)
db_rdl.what: A hip hinge that strengthens your hamstrings, bottom and lower back.
steps: Stand holding the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees slightly - they stay at this bend.
Push your hips backwards and slide the weights down your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the back of your thighs (around knee to mid-shin).
Push your hips forward to stand tall.
tips: It's a hinge, not a squat - your hips move back, your knees barely change.
Keep the weights close to your legs.
db_rdl.cue: Hips back, flat back, weights close to legs

step_up.name: Step Up
step_up.equipment: A low, stable step or box (start 20-30 cm)
step_up.what: Single-leg strength that mimics climbing and running.
steps: Place your whole foot on the step.
Push through that foot to stand up tall on the step.
Lower the other foot back to the floor slowly.
Do all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Use a rail for balance. Push with the top leg - don't spring off the bottom one.
step_up.cue: Push through the top foot. Step down slowly

reverse_nordic.name: Reverse Nordic (optional)
reverse_nordic.what: Stretches and strengthens the front of the thigh at the same time - aimed at the tight, sore stretch.
steps: Kneel upright on a padded mat, knees hip-width apart.
Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lean back slowly a short way (start with a small lean).
Use your thigh muscles to pull yourself back upright.
tips: Only do it if your quad stretch test is 2/10 or less. Skip it on any amber day.
Lean back a little further only when the current range feels easy.
reverse_nordic.cue: Lean back a little, body straight, come up

sauna.name: Sauna / Steam / Jacuzzi
sauna.what: Your reward for turning up. Optional - but if it keeps you coming back, it is doing its job.
steps: Drink water before going in.
Stay 10-15 minutes. Sit on a lower, cooler bench if it feels too hot.
Cool down and drink water afterwards.
tips: Leave straight away if you feel dizzy or unwell.
Skip it after alcohol or if you are ill.
sauna.cue: 10–15 min. Drink water. Leave if dizzy
